source_caption:
Inspired by Charlotte Wells’ memories of her relationship with her father, Aftersun (2022) is a quietly devastating film about memory, love, and the things we only begin to understand later in life.

Set in the late 1990s, the story follows 11-year-old Sophie spending a summer holiday at a Turkish resort with her young father, Calum. As Sophie records parts of their trip on a camcorder, the film captures small, ordinary moments between them that slowly reveal a deeper emotional weight.

Years later, an adult Sophie looks back on those memories, trying to understand the man her father really was.

Starring Paul Mescal and Frankie Corio, the film was widely praised for its emotional subtlety, with Mescal receiving an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor. Through its quiet storytelling, the film turns a simple holiday into a powerful reflection on memory and the fragile bond between a parent and child.

source_details.synopsis: Aftersun is a 2022 independent semi-autobiographical coming-of-age drama film written and directed by Charlotte Wells in her feature directorial debut. Starring Paul Mescal, Frankie Corio, and Celia Rowlson-Hall, the film is loosely based on Wells' childhood and follows an 11-year-old Scottish girl on holiday with her father at a Turkish resort on the eve of his 31st birthday. Aftersun had its world premiere at the Cannes Film Festival on 21 May 2022, where Wells was nominated for the Caméra d'Or.
